summary: Ahead of the Supreme Court's review of the stray-dog case, the [Kerala, Goa and Jharkhand High Courts](#feature) have stepped up pressure on local bodies, rejecting excuses for the lack of shelters, ordering action against defaulting officials and opening a fresh case on animals on highways.
The [Supreme Court](#courts) has said future transfers of captive elephants must strictly follow its earlier directions, after five elephants were moved in haste from Assam to temples in Tamil Nadu.

The window for objections to the [draft rules on laboratory animals](#movement) closed on November 5, with scientists, veterinarians, lawmakers and more than 60 organisations calling for their withdrawal. The Centre is yet to respond.

OpenAI's revised [Model Spec](#world), released on October 29, reportedly asks its AI models to take animals into account for the first time. On the [EA Forum](#forum), researcher Lotte de Lint examines why academia produces so little reliable evidence on reducing meat consumption.

cover.title: Stray dogs: High Courts tighten the screws ahead of Supreme Court review
cover.dek: Acting on directions issued by the Supreme Court in May, the Kerala High Court has held that local opposition is no excuse for failing to build shelters, the Bombay High Court at Goa has ordered disciplinary action against officials who repeatedly missed deadlines, and the Jharkhand High Court has opened a case of its own on stray dogs and cattle on highways. Their compliance reports will feed into the Supreme Court's review, reportedly listed for November 17.

topStories.title: Objections close as calls for withdrawal grow
topStories.text: Scientists, veterinarians, MPs, actors and more than 60 groups have urged the Centre to withdraw G.S.R. 864(E). No extension has been announced.

topStories.text: The Bench declined to order the return of five elephants to Assam, but said future transfers must strictly follow its directions.

topStories.title: OpenAI's rulebook for its AI now mentions animals
topStories.text: Reviewers say the October 29 update is the first to ask OpenAI's models to weigh the effect of their answers on animals.

feature.title: High Courts step in to enforce the Supreme Court's stray-dog order
feature.dek: In its May 2026 judgment in the nationwide stray-dog case, the Supreme Court asked the High Courts to monitor how States carry out its directions. Over the past fortnight, three of them have shown what that oversight looks like in practice. The [Kerala High Court](https://www.livelaw.in/high-court/kerala-high-court/kerala-high-court-joint-shelters-for-stray-dogs-panchayats-identify-suitable-land-556530) rejected the explanations offered by local bodies, the [Bombay High Court at Goa](https://nenews.in/goa/goa-hc-orders-disciplinary-action-against-8-panchayat-secretaries-over-stray-dog-reports/70158/) turned its attention to individual officials, and the [Jharkhand High Court](https://www.thehansindia.com/news/national/jharkhand-hc-seeks-compliance-report-from-state-centre-over-stray-dogs-and-cattle-on-roads-1139521) opened a fresh case on its own.

items.text: Local bodies told the court they could not find land for shelters or had faced resistance from residents. The Bench held that public opposition did not justify non-compliance, and warned that defaulters could face contempt proceedings before the Supreme Court.
The court allowed two or three panchayats to set up a common shelter.
Dogs removed from public premises must be released as the Supreme Court directed, neither returned to those premises nor kept in shelters in breach of its order.

The Kochi Corporation was asked to explain how it runs its Animal Birth Control programme. Advocates Shruthi Bhat and Pooja Omanakuttan were appointed amici curiae, and the Registry was to send a consolidated compliance report to the Supreme Court by November 6.

Noting what it called “clear remissness”, including on the part of the Panaji Corporation, the Bombay High Court at Goa directed the Directors of Panchayats and Municipal Administration to begin disciplinary action against officials who had repeatedly failed to comply. Contempt proceedings remain open separately ([Daijiworld](https://daijiworld.com/news/newsDisplay?newsID=1333598)).

The court ordered disciplinary proceedings against the secretaries of eight panchayats that had not filed reports, giving them a final opportunity to do so by November 16. The Animal Husbandry Department has until December 1 to submit an action plan for shelters.

Taking suo motu cognisance of the risk to road users from stray dogs and cattle on roads and national highways, the court sought responses from the Centre and the State, along with a compliance report. The matter will be heard next on December 3.

facts.label: Kerala case
facts.text: In Re: Compliance with the Directions issued by the Supreme Court in SMWP (C) No. 5 of 2025 · W.P.(C) No. 23376/2026 · Dr. Justice A.K. Jayasankaran Nambiar and Justice Preeta A.K.

facts.label: Goa case
facts.text: Suo Motu Writ Petition No. 2 of 2026 (title as reported by [LiveLaw on 14 Oct](https://www.livelaw.in/high-court/bombay-high-court/goa-civic-officials-contempt-proceedings-delay-data-collection-554567)) · Justices Valmiki Menezes and Amit S. Jamsandekar

facts.label: Supreme Court
facts.text: Main judgment of May 19, 2026, 2026 SCC OnLine SC 894 ([SCC Online summary](https://www.scconline.com/blog/post/2026/05/19/sc-stray-dogs-abc-rules-nationwide-sterilisation-directions-may-2026/)). A review of compliance by the States is reportedly listed for November 17, subject to the cause list.

facts.label: Awaited
facts.text: The outcomes of stray-dog hearings in the Delhi (November 3), Madhya Pradesh (November 3) and Allahabad (affidavits due November 5) High Courts had not been reported at the time of writing.

feature.whyItMatters: Directions from the Supreme Court carry weight only if someone ensures that municipalities and panchayats follow them. The High Courts have now taken up that task, and they are holding named officials to account rather than issuing general orders. For advocates, these hearings offer a forum to raise problems on the ground, from absent sterilisation programmes to substandard shelters and dogs released in violation of the order. The compliance reports headed to the Supreme Court will shape its next steps, which makes local evidence filed now all the more important.

cases.title: Captive elephant transfers must follow rules, says Supreme Court
cases.citation: Petition by People for Cattle in India (PFCI) · Supreme Court · CJI Surya Kant & Justice Joymalya Bagchi · hearing on November 5 · case number not reported; linked to the pending captive-elephant case W.P.(C) 743/2014

parts.label: Background
parts.text: People for Cattle in India (PFCI) challenged the transfer of five captive elephants from Assam to temples in Tamil Nadu. Its counsel told the court that one elephant had been moved about 3,000 km in nine days, a process that normally takes around 50.

parts.label: The ruling
parts.text: As all five elephants had already been moved, the Bench said it could not order their return. It held that future transfers must strictly comply with statutory requirements and its earlier directions on verifying identity and ownership, and that neither High Courts nor State governments may act contrary to them. PFCI withdrew the petition, with liberty to raise the issue in the pending case.

parts.label: Significance
parts.text: Long-distance transfers of elephants to temples have proved hard to halt once under way. The Bench's reminder gives petitioners firmer ground to challenge the next one early.

cases.title: Madras High Court orders closure of 87 illegal resorts in Sathyamangalam Tiger Reserve
cases.citation: Dr. R. Karpagam v. Principal Chief Conservator of Forests & Chief Wildlife Warden · WP No. 13711 of 2022 · 2026 LiveLaw (Mad) 527 · Madras High Court · Justices N. Sathish Kumar & G.K. Muthukumar · order date not stated

parts.label: Background
parts.text: The Erode Collector informed the court that 87 resorts were operating inside the reserve, none with planning or building approval and none with permission from the hill-area authority for a change in land use.

parts.label: The ruling
parts.text: The court ordered all illegal structures to be closed immediately, with steps towards demolition, and directed that unlicensed resorts be locked and sealed. It also found that two resorts which had obtained interim protection from another Bench, without disclosing the pending case, had not approached the court with clean hands.

parts.label: Significance
parts.text: Tourism construction inside tiger reserves puts steady pressure on wildlife habitat, and the order is unusually sweeping in its effort to reverse it.

cases.title: Supreme Court sends Nahargarh sanctuary boundary dispute to Rajasthan High Court
cases.citation: Rajendra Tiwari v. Union of India & Ors · Civil Appeal No. 13859/2026 · Supreme Court · CJI Surya Kant, Justices Joymalya Bagchi & V. Mohana

parts.label: Background
parts.text: The appeal, filed against an order of the National Green Tribunal, challenged the revised boundaries of the Nahargarh Wildlife Sanctuary near Jaipur.

parts.label: The ruling
parts.text: Without going into the merits, the court directed the appellant to the Rajasthan High Court, where the revised map is already under challenge, and asked it to consider all objections on how the reserve forest and sanctuary areas are identified. The Bench also asked why a monitoring committee's report had not been placed before the tribunal.

cases.title: Madhya Pradesh High Court orders probe into two more tiger deaths in Kanha
cases.citation: Subit Chakraborty v. Union of India · WP 19398 of 2026 · Madhya Pradesh High Court (Jabalpur) · Chief Justice Alpesh Y. Kogje & Justice Vivek Jain · order date not stated

parts.label: The ruling
parts.text: The court directed the State to investigate two further deaths of tigers in the Kanha Tiger Reserve and to file a report within two weeks. The case will be heard next on November 16.

cases.title: Radhanpur drops four-month closure of meat shops before Gujarat High Court
cases.citation: 2026 LiveLaw (Guj) 302 · Gujarat High Court · Justice Nikhil S. Kariel

parts.label: Background
parts.text: The Radhanpur Municipality had ordered slaughterhouses, meat shops and non-vegetarian restaurants to remain shut for four months during the stay of a Jain religious leader in the town.

parts.label: Outcome
parts.text: Before the court, the municipality conceded that no legal provision supported the order and said it would not press its decisions of August 17. The petition was withdrawn with liberty to approach the court again.

parts.label: Significance
parts.text: Though not an animal-welfare ruling, the case is a reminder that blanket closures of meat businesses need a basis in law.

justBefore.title: J&K High Court: cattle-theft cases do not justify preventive detention
justBefore.text: In Tariq Ahmad Dar v. UT of J&K (LPA No. 254/2026), a Bench of Chief Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati and Justice Mohd Yousuf Wani quashed a detention under the Public Safety Act that rested on cattle-theft FIRs, holding that such cases were matters of law and order that ordinary criminal law could address. The ruling, reported on October 25, adds to a series of similar decisions from the court this year.

quiet: Outcomes awaited: the Delhi High Court's stray-dog hearing on November 3, the Madhya Pradesh High Court's review on the same day, the Allahabad High Court's matter on dog-bite hotspots, in which affidavits were due on November 5, and the Madras High Court's listing on temple elephants on October 30 had not been reported at the time of writing.

No new central notifications were found from the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, the Environment Ministry, the AWBI, the Central Zoo Authority, the NTCA or the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau, and the Centre has not responded to objections on the laboratory-animal rules. Shortly before this period, the [Animal Feeds and Feed Ingredients (Quality Control) Order, 2026](https://www.scconline.com/blog/post/2026/10/16/animal-feeds-feed-ingredients-quality-control-order-2026-bis-certification/) made BIS certification mandatory (reported October 16). FSSAI is reported to have approved a fermentation-derived mycelium ingredient on October 27, according to a [vegconomist listing](https://vegconomist.com/category/cultivated-cell-cultured-biotechnology/approvals/); the details could not be independently confirmed.

No animal-law ruling from the National Green Tribunal was reported in this period, and there has been no movement on the Kerala Wildlife Protection (Amendment) Bill, which the Centre told Parliament in August it could not accept.

movement.tag: PETA India, Peedu's People and others · Draft laboratory rules
movement.title: Objections close on draft lab-animal rules amid calls for withdrawal
movement.text: The period for objections to the draft Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (Control and Supervision of Experiment, Breeding and Trading of Laboratory Animals) Rules, 2026, notified as G.S.R. 864(E) on October 6, closed on November 5, according to [MedBound Times](https://www.medboundtimes.com/daily-pulse/gsr-864-e-draft-animal-experimentation-rules-2026-objections) and most other reports. In the final days, scientists, veterinarians, legislators across parties and more than 60 organisations sought the withdrawal of the rules ([Telangana Today, November 3](https://telanganatoday.com/scientists-animal-welfare-groups-demand-withdrawal-of-draft-animal-testing-rules)). Their objections centre on the self-approval of experiments by in-house ethics committees, exemptions for wild-caught and stray animals, and inspections with advance notice. PETA India says more than 18,000 people, along with several actors and MPs, back its campaign ([OrissaPOST/PTI, November 2](https://www.orissapost.com/?p=904809)). Peedu's People joined a student march in Pune on October 29 ([Punekar News](https://www.punekarnews.in/?p=248065)), and former Assam Leader of the Opposition Debabrata Saikia filed a formal objection ([Sentinel, October 26](https://www.sentinelassam.com/north-east-india-news/assam-news/assam-debabrata-saikia-seeks-withdrawal-of-animal-experiment-rules)). In a [piece for LiveLaw](https://www.livelaw.in/articles/self-approval-another-name-2026draft-animal-testing-rules-pca-act-556696) on November 1, Shreya Bajpai argues that the draft fails the test of Section 17 of the PCA Act and calls for targeted amendments. No extension or official response has been announced.

movement.tag: Humane World for Animals India · Stray dogs
movement.title: Training centre for Animal Birth Control staff opens in Lucknow
movement.text: Uttar Pradesh's Urban Development Minister inaugurated the centre at Jarhara, set up by the Lucknow Municipal Corporation and the Animal Welfare Board of India and run by Humane World for Animals India under a three-year agreement, the organisation said in a statement. It offers a 15-day course for veterinarians, para-veterinarians and dog handlers working in sterilisation programmes. The organisation describes it as the first such centre in the country and says more than one lakh dogs in Lucknow have been sterilised and vaccinated since 2019. The opening comes as the courts step up scrutiny of ABC compliance (see [Feature](#feature)).

movement.title: ALPN maps community-dog services in Mumbai and Thane
movement.text: The Animal Law and Policy Network has mapped the NGOs and government veterinary services working with community dogs in Mumbai Suburban and Thane, and assessed eight interventions, among them sterilisation, vaccination and shelters. The study is meant to help funders and NGOs direct money and effort where it will do the most good. ALPN lists the work among its ongoing projects and has not given a publication date.

movement.tag: Humane World for Animals India · Dog-meat trade
movement.title: 26 dogs rescued from truck in Assam
movement.text: Police in Karbi Anglong intercepted a truck carrying 26 dogs packed in sacks, suspected to be bound for the dog-meat trade, according to a statement from Humane World for Animals India. Local groups including Just Be Friendly (JBF) took part in the rescue, and the dogs were taken to JBF's centre in Guwahati. The statement does not say whether an FIR was registered.

movement.title: Plant-based meat outperforms chicken on absorbable protein, finds lab study
movement.text: A study by GFI India and CSIR-IHBT, which tested five commercial products using simulated digestion, found protein bioavailability of 57-86% in plant-based products against 21-43% in chicken. The authors caution that laboratory results may not reflect absorption in the human body. The report also notes that India imports nearly 90% of its plant protein isolates, a gap that domestic industry has yet to fill.

movement.title: Fortified feed speeds fish growth but does not improve welfare, finds FWI
movement.text: Fish Welfare Initiative compared a fortified pellet feed with de-oiled rice bran on 12 farms in Nellore, building on earlier pond and tank trials. Fish on the fortified feed gained 73% more weight, but water quality, health and stress levels did not differ, and about 45% of early-morning oxygen readings fell below 3 mg/L regardless of the feed. As the feed also cost farmers more, FWI has decided against building a programme around it and has published the results openly. Its [grants call for India](#careers) closes on November 18.

movement.title: ACE to announce 2026 charity recommendations
movement.text: Animal Charity Evaluators will name its recommended charities on November 10. This year's evaluations covered Aquatic Life Institute, Kafessiz Türkiye, Dansk Vegetarisk Forening, Sinergia Animal, Crustacean Compassion and Greener by Default, none of which is described as working in India. The results will be covered in the next issue.

pick.label: Pick of the fortnight
pick.title: Takes on why academia underproduces high-quality evidence on reducing animal product consumption
pick.author: Lotte de Lint
pick.text: Lotte de Lint, a PhD researcher at Wageningen University, sets out six ways in which academic incentives work against useful evidence on diet change. Studies often fail to answer the questions advocates face, concentrate on health and climate rather than animals, and are largely confined to Western countries. Interventions that are easy to test crowd out more promising ones, and field data on actual behaviour goes unrewarded. Of 637 outcomes in one library of studies, more than half measured intentions or attitudes rather than behaviour. Her point about the Western focus of research is especially relevant to India, where there is little local evidence on which to base campaigns.

posts.title: We tested 14 meat-reduction messages with real money at stake. Celebrities and history did best.
posts.author: Laura Thomas-Walters
posts.text: In an online experiment with 4,761 Americans, researchers measured how much participants valued a plant-based gift basket after reading short messages. Appeals to being on the 'right side of history' and messages featuring celebrities had the strongest effect, while those citing trends or pandemics made little difference. The study measured a single choice made immediately after the message rather than any lasting change in diet, and its sample was limited to the United States.

posts.title: Votos Pelos Animais: How Farmed Animal Policy Wins Votes In Brazil
posts.author: JLRiedi (Faunalytics)
posts.text: A survey experiment with 1,908 Brazilian adults tested nine policy proposals on farmed animals. A ban on clearing the Amazon and Cerrado for industrial animal farming and tougher penalties for cruelty to farmed animals drew the most support, while every proposal favouring the industry fell below 50%. A similar study could prove valuable ahead of State elections in India.

posts.title: An ASI that's bad for animal welfare is probably bad for humans, too
posts.author: Michael Dickens
posts.text: Michael Dickens argues that a superintelligent AI aligned with human preferences yet harmful to animals is a narrow target, since an AI that simply satisfied human preferences would also produce outcomes that are terrible for many people. Getting AI values right, he concludes, matters for humans and animals alike. The piece is a useful companion to the [item on OpenAI's Model Spec](#world).

careers.intro: Paid roles, grants and training open to people in India, all confirmed as open on November 9. Fish Welfare Initiative has three openings in India this fortnight, and GFI APAC is recruiting for senior roles across the region, including a [Head of Policy](https://gfi.org/resource/head-of-policy/).

items.title: Grants for new ideas on farmed fish welfare in India
items.location: Open to anyone; the work must be relevant to Indian aquaculture
items.text: Standard grants of up to ₹10 lakh are on offer, rising to ₹50 lakh for exceptional proposals. Academics, companies, NGOs and individuals may apply using FWI's template; basic research will be funded only if it links to a possible FWI programme.

items.title: Understanding how people (actually) make decisions
items.location: Online · 1.30 p.m. or 8.30 p.m. IST (8 a.m. or 3 p.m. UK) · 90 minutes
items.text: A free introduction to behavioural science for campaigners and for staff in corporate relations and communications. The session covers how people make decisions, the two systems of thinking, a framework for building stronger messages and a few biases that can be applied right away, with examples such as winning a cage-free commitment or getting a petition signed. Registrants will receive a recording. The registration pages do not name an organiser, so participants should confirm the timings when they sign up.

items.title: Strategic Advisor on Food Security
items.location: Remote, ideally in or near a focus region (including South/Southeast Asia), with regular overlap with CET hours
items.text: The adviser will lead ProVeg's food-security strategy in one region, steering the growth in protein supply towards plant-rich and alternative sources. The role is for 30-40 hours a week, ideally on a 12-month freelance contract.

items.title: Director of Digital Campaigns
items.location: Fully remote, anywhere (must be able to work legally where you live; no visa sponsorship)
items.deadline: November 30, 2026, end of day (time zone not stated)
items.text: The role involves running digital tactics, including mass emails, online actions and creative material, in campaigns that press food companies on farmed-animal welfare. Applicants need at least three years' experience; pay for those outside the United States is discussed at interview.

items.title: Sustainable Poultry Supply Chain Engagement Manager (India)
items.location: India, work from home with some travel
items.text: The manager will work to persuade medium and large egg producers to switch to cage-free systems. The role calls for at least two years in sales or a similar field and fluency in Telugu or Tamil, with Hindi strongly preferred.

items.title: Welfare Measurement Lead
items.location: Indian nationals only · Eluru, Andhra Pradesh for at least 6 months of year one, otherwise remote within India
items.text: A senior role building FWI's systems for welfare measurement and for monitoring and evaluation, designing farm studies and managing one or two field staff. The salary is ₹1.3-2.7 lakh a month.

items.title: Human Resources Manager
items.location: Right to work in India required · remote, with a preference for time at the Eluru office
items.text: The role covers recruitment, employee relations, compliance and training, working closely with the Managing Director. The salary is ₹50,000-90,000 a month.

items.title: Centenary Research Award
items.location: Worldwide; lead applicant must be at a host research institute or organisation
items.text: The award offers up to £250,000 for a two- to four-year project on a major animal-welfare challenge. Full proposals are due on May 15, 2027.

items.title: OpenAI's Model Spec asks AI models to consider animals
items.text: OpenAI released an updated Model Spec, the set of rules its AI models follow, on October 29. According to reviews by [Ariel Simnegar](https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/SYprbthckE7pcxPFz/ariel-simnegar-s-quick-takes?commentId=EAdxtd5FHewWuBM7A) and [Zvi Mowshowitz](https://thezvi.substack.com/p/openai-updates-its-model-spec), the side effects that models are asked to weigh now include effects on “other people, animals, or the environment”. In one new example, a model asked to find a Scottish Fold breeder mentions the welfare problems associated with the breed; in another, it is told to consider the animals living in a park that is being redesigned. Simnegar describes it as the first version to explicitly ask the models to weigh animal welfare. The wording could not be independently checked against the Spec.

items.title: End the Cage Age proposals missing from EU's 2027 work programme
items.text: The European Commission's work programme for 2027, published on November 4, makes no mention of the promised laws on the welfare of laying hens, broilers and pigs, which formed part of its End the Cage Age commitments. A proposal on poultry may still come in December 2026; no explanation has been offered on the one for pigs.

items.title: Portugal bans permanent chaining of animals
items.text: Portugal's Parliament on October 28 passed Bills banning the permanent tethering of animals, their long-term confinement on balconies and the use of restraint or training equipment that causes unnecessary pain. The law awaits presidential assent, after which implementing rules must be framed within 90 days.

items.title: U.K. clears cultivated beef, but only for pet food
items.text: Ivy Farm Technologies on November 5 won approval to sell cultivated Wagyu beef as an ingredient in pet food in the United Kingdom. Its applications to sell the product for human consumption in the U.K., the European Union and the United States are pending.
